abstract: Monosomy-X results in Turner Syndrome (TS), which beyond its cardinal height and reproductive phenotypes, spans incompletely penetrant cardiovascular phenotypes, including bicuspid valve, hypoplastic left-sided heart syndrome and aortic coarctation. These congenital heart defects (CHD) conspire with hypertension to dilate the ascending aorta, which can progress to rupture and drive early mortality in TS. Genetic contributors to incompletely penetrant phenotypes in TS remain only partially explored, thus complicating risk stratification. To begin addressing this challenge in donor-specific in-vitro models, we derived monosomy-X human induced pluripotent stem cells (hiPSCs) alongside isogenic euploid control lines from donors mosaic for the second sex chromosome. In embryonic-origin specific vascular smooth muscle cells (vSMCs) derived from these hiPSCs, monosomy-X reveals donor-specific cellular and transcriptomic effects, with expression changes in one donor panel enriched in genes previously implicated in coronary artery disease and ascending aorta diameter. Polygenic risk scores (PGS) for cardiovascular traits mirror this transcriptomic enrichment, and suggest PGS analysis may help to prioritize hiPSC lines for in-vitro modeling of incompletely-penetrant traits related to TS-associated aortopathy.
